lines.li: [us] You're from {TOWN}, the {POSTKIND} your people opened near us?
[them,their:tribal] Yes, the elders sent us out so your people would not have so far to walk.
[them,their:medieval] Aye, the market at {TOWN}, and a fair one, ask anyone.
[them,their:spacer] Correct, the ground station handles our trade in this region.
[them] That's right, it saves all of us a long haul.
[us] Is it doing well?
[them,town:struggling|town:poor] Slowly, we need more buyers than we have.
[them,!town:struggling,!town:poor] Well enough, and better when your caravans come.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: {PEOPLE} keep a {POSTKIND} at {TOWN}, opened to trade with the colony.

lines.li: [us] Why open a {POSTKIND} out here, so far from your own towns?
[them] Because your people kept coming all that way, and that's worth a roof and a counter.
[us] We're glad of it.
[them,their:tribal] Then bring good hides, and the fire there will stay lit.
[them] Then keep trading with us, and it will stay open.
[them] {KEEPER} keeps the books at {TOWN} and counts every bolt of cloth twice.
[us] Is that a complaint?
[them] Only on the days I'm the one carrying the cloth.
[them] The road between {TOWN} and our own towns is long, and robbers know it.
[us] Is it safe?
[them,their:lowtech] Safe enough with spears along, and the spears are why we price as we do.
[them] Safe enough with guards, and the guards are why we price the way we do.
[them] Trade at {TOWN} has been thin, and the {POSTKIND} barely pays its way.
[us] What would help?
[them] Buyers, mostly, and your people are the nearest we have.
[them] {TOWN} does better than anyone back home thought it would.
[us] Will it grow into a proper town?
[them] It's a {POSTKIND}, not a town, but nobody there minds the extra coin.
[them] {KEEPER} says we may have to close {TOWN} unless things mend between us.
[them] There's talk at {TOWN} of packing up unless things mend between us.
[us] We'd rather it stayed.
[them,tone:warm|tone:good] So would I, so let's both see that it does.
[them] So would I, but it isn't up to me.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: {PEOPLE} may close {TOWN} unless things mend with the colony.

lines.li: [them] Our camps move with the seasons back home, but the trading camp stays for you.
[us] Why stay?
[them] Because you keep coming, and the elders say a good path should be kept open.
[them] The market at {TOWN} pays its dues to our lord like any other.
[us] And what do you get for it?
[them] Peace on the road, mostly, when the lord remembers us.
[them] The depot at {TOWN} runs on ledgers and patience.
[us] Which runs out first?
[them] Patience, every time, ask any clerk.
[us] The Empire keeps a station this close to us now?
[them] The Empire keeps what serves it, and trade with your colony serves it for now.
[us] For now?
[them] Everything is for now, until the court says otherwise.
[them] Our people keep a {POSTKIND} at {POST}, nearer to you than my own town.
[us] We know it.
[them] Good, then you won't have to walk half so far to find our goods.
[them] I hear {POSTPEOPLE} have opened a trading post at {POST}, close to you.
[us] They have.
[them,role:trader] Then I'll have to keep my prices honest, it seems.
[them] A market close by is a fine thing to have.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: {POSTPEOPLE} keep a trading post at {POST}, near the colony.

lines.li: [us] Have you been to {POST}, the post {POSTPEOPLE} keep near us?
[them,their:empire] The Empire does its own trading, thank you.
[them] Not yet, but I hear they pay fair prices.
